stem: During an investigation, an officer gets a suspect to confess by threatening him. Under Article III, Section 12 of the 1987 Constitution, how may this confession be used?
choices: It cannot be used in evidence against him.
It can be used once the suspect signs it.
It can be used if a judge approves it later.
It can be used, but only with other evidence.
answer: It cannot be used in evidence against him.
hints: Notice how the confession was obtained: by a threat.
Section 12 bans "torture, force, violence, threat, intimidation" against a person under investigation. Next, find what it says about a confession obtained that way.

Section 12 has a sentence about "Any confession or admission obtained in violation of this" section. Read the word that describes such a confession, then pick the choice that means the same. Check whether the section gives any exception for signing, a judge's approval or other evidence.

solution.methodName: Match the situation to the provision

steps.action: Identify the right involved: the rights of a person under investigation, in Article III, Section 12.
steps.why: The suspect is being investigated for an offense, which is exactly who Section 12 protects.

steps.action: Check whether the officer broke Section 12: "No torture, force, violence, threat, intimidation, or any other means which vitiate the free will shall be used against him."
steps.why: A threat is named in the list. "Vitiate the free will" means to spoil a person's free choice.

steps.action: Read the rule on such confessions: "Any confession or admission obtained in violation of this or Section 17 hereof shall be inadmissible in evidence against him."
steps.why: "Inadmissible" means it cannot be accepted or used as evidence.

steps.action: Note that the section gives no exception for signing, a judge's approval or other evidence.
The confession cannot be used in evidence against him.

trapNotes.It can be used once the suspect signs it: Signing does not fix a confession obtained by threat. Section 12 makes any confession obtained in violation of the section inadmissible.
trapNotes.It can be used if a judge approves it la: Section 12 gives no exception for a judge's approval. A confession obtained in violation of the section is inadmissible.
trapNotes.It can be used, but only with other evid: Other evidence may exist, but this confession itself stays inadmissible. Section 12 does not allow it to be used against him at all.
